fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is bulk Co/Ni alloying of high-strength steel, whereas the target intervention is atmospheric-plasma deposition of an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L followed by a 550 °C anneal.
The proposed aqueous, moderate-temperature chloride conditions do not reconstruct either the 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemical test or the 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion tests.

The cited evidence concerns AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloy in NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 molten salt at 450–650 °C, so it does not establish that adding Co and Ni to conventional steels produces the claimed mechanism in aqueous chemical-processing or nuclear environments.

The hypothesis attributes protection primarily to Co/Ni enrichment while omitting the target's central Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides, coating barrier, annealing-induced densification and grain refinement, and pore-mediated degradation.

The proposed mechanism depends on redox behavior involving Al/Cr depletion and molten-salt impurities in the cited study; it cannot be transferred to a Co/Ni-modified steel lacking those redox couples without additional evidence.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance and offers a controlled comparison with surface analysis, electrochemistry, and an explicit falsification rule, so it has some general problem alignment and good experimental testability. However, it does not reconstruct the material, coating process, annealing treatment, exposure conditions, baselines, or governing mechanism of the target. Its evidence shows Co/Ni enrichment in an Al-containing high-entropy alloy under high-temperature molten-chloride corrosion, not in bulk-Co/Ni-modified steels under moderate aqueous chloride exposure. Thus the central extrapolation is not adequately supported. The experiment could test the proposed alternative, but composition changes would also alter phase structure and passivity, so it would need matched alloys and film-depth-resolved controls to attribute any benefit specifically to self-enrichment.
